title: Spandana Sphoorty Financial Ltd - 542759 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Spandana Q2 FY27: AUM up 10% QoQ to INR5,364 crore, GNPA down to 2.5% and PAT of INR18 crore, with Maharashtra drought stress the key watch item.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a good quarter, the third in a row of improvement. AUM rose about 10% QoQ to INR5,364 crore, disbursements were INR1,481 crore with 54% to new customers, and about 1.5 lakh new borrowers were added. Yield rose to 24.9% and marginal cost of borrowing fell to 10.6% (10.8% excluding CGS), lifting NIM to 13.6%. Reported PAT was INR18 crore, including a one-time INR7.9 crore DTA reversal linked to the CFL merger, and GNPA fell to 2.5% partly due to an ARC sale. Management flagged Maharashtra (and to a lesser extent Karnataka) as stressed by drought, with 18 of 127 Maharashtra branches classed as critical.

financial_highlights.change: 54% to new customers, 11% to reactivated dropouts, 35% to existing customers
vs INR12 crore in Q1; includes INR7.9 crore one-time DTA reversal
vs 96.2% low point over last 2 years

financial_highlights.value: INR1,622 crore incl. INR995 crore CGS

segments.name: Microfinance (JLG, parent Spandana)
segments.commentary: Parent book is 100% qualifying assets; 96% of the MFI book was originated under the new guardrails. Borrowers per branch up 8% and borrowers per loan officer up 15% to 211.

segments.name: Criss Financial (CFL, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mix of individual loans and micro-LAP; LAP book about INR305 crore across 6 states, targeted at INR1,000 crore in 2-3 years. Ticket size moving to INR5-15/20 lakh with 7-10 year tenor, about 60-65% LTV and 19-22% pricing; about 70 exclusive LAP branches.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement guidance of INR6,000-6,500 crore, AUM above INR6,000 crore and opex around INR675 crore unchanged as of end-October; management said it will not give a false commitment if conditions change.
Gross credit cost guided at 2.5-3% of book; net credit cost guidance for H2 not given, with management calling it too early given stress in certain states.
AUM target of about INR10,000 crore by March 2028.
Long-term BAU ROA of 3.5-4% from FY27 onwards, with ROE around 14-15% at about 4x gearing.
Next capital raise expected around middle of next year if the plan proceeds.
CFL merger awaiting regulator nod, expected in 3-4 months; new LOS migration of branches to complete over next couple of months.
Management expects December-January to bring clarity on drought impact; November should show first signals.
capex_capacity: New LOS piloted; full branch migration targeted over the next couple of months.
LAP business run through about 86 branches, to be reduced to about 70-75 exclusive LAP branches over next couple of months.
Leadership restructuring with leaner structure in certain geographies, with senior people at top.
No new states planned for at least the next year; growth within the existing 6 LAP states (Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu).
demand_pricing: October business and disbursements described as steady; Maharashtra recoveries need extra effort, while Andhra, Telangana and Karnataka are not an issue as of now.
In Maharashtra, 127 branches classified into A-D risk categories; 18 critical branches get special focus, with curbs on new-to-credit onboarding and stricter norms for new-to-Spandana customers.
Book in Karnataka and Maharashtra is about INR600 crore combined, with 96% current and 3% GNPA.
Average ticket size has moved to about INR45,000 to be in line with market.
Management sees industry growth of 10-25% p.a. as calibrated, not 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: What are October collection trends and disbursement momentum, particularly in drought-hit areas?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the month looked steady on business and recoveries; growth is not being slowed, with Maharashtra needing more recovery effort while other southern states are fine.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any drought or excess rain impact beyond Maharashtra?
qa_highlights.answer: Rains in Odisha, Andhra and Telangana are too early to judge; management sees no major stress as of month-end and expects about 3 months for recovery in affected areas.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost guidance changing, given the provisions this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross credit cost is guided at 2.5-3%, net of recoveries could be nil or marginally positive; H2 net guidance was not given as the situation is still evolving.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the GNPA decline, and what is the new-book GNPA?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of the GNPA decline came from an ARC sale in the subsidiary, with a smaller underlying reduction; loans disbursed since 1 April 2025 show about 0.5% GNPA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10.6% cost of debt inclusive of CGS?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 10.6% includes CGS funds; excluding CGS it is 10.8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY29 ROA/ROE and sector growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 3.5-4% ROA and about 14-15% ROE in the BAU phase from FY27, with sector growth of 10-25% p.a. and an AUM target of INR10,000 crore by March 2028.

risks_watch: Maharashtra drought stress: 18 critical branches, recoveries requiring extra effort; signals expected in November, clarity by December-January.
Consolidated GNPA of 2.5% flattered partly by an ARC sale; underlying trend needs watching next quarter.
Credit cost: gross 2.5-3% guided, with H2 net guidance not given.
Regulatory or merger timeline for CFL (3-4 months expected) and migration of new LOS.
Next capital raise expected around mid-2027; leverage target around 4x.
Opex: management says overall opex will not rise despite reinvestment in collections and 90+ bucket staffing.
Qualifying asset norm (75% now, possibly reduced to 68% or 50%) if regulation changes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the recovery and business momentum, but noticeably cautious on Maharashtra and the drought, repeatedly saying it is too early to quantify and declining to give H2 net credit cost guidance. Management was assertive on the long-term ROA target and deflected on near-term precision.
key_quotes: So as of now, it is holding good, but gross could be hovering between 2.5% to 3%.
Simple business, just stay focused on basics.
You can't talk about a 40%, 50% growth, but 10%, 15%, 20% or 25%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM rose 10% QoQ to INR5,364 crore, FY27 disbursement guidance of INR6,000-6,500 crore is held, and AUM target is about INR10,000 crore by March 2028, though Maharashtra needs extra recovery effort.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Maharashtra has 18 of 127 branches classed as critical, and H2 net credit cost guidance was not given; management expects clarity on the drought impact only in December-January.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CFL LAP book is about INR305 crore across 6 states with a target of INR1,000 crore in 2-3 years, and ticket sizes are moving to INR5-20 lakh with 7-10 year tenor.

rows.label: CFL merger approval
rows.why: CFL merger is awaiting regulator nod, expected in 3-4 months, and the new LOS migration of branches completes over the next couple of months.

rows.label: Growth within six existing LAP states only
rows.why: No new states are planned for at least the next year; growth stays within Rajasthan, MP, AP, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

tone.note: Management was confident on recovery, the NIM rise and the held FY27 guidance, but cautious on Maharashtra drought stress and declined to give H2 net credit cost guidance; analysts pushed on the drought, credit costs and how much of the GNPA fall came from the ARC sale.
